name: Dominic Cho
life: “I still remember knocking at the old school after the desks were sold.” Saturday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Dominic takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I am returning a book to a closed classroom. The retired teacher offered to meet me at the till.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Dominic has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. Dominic grins on one side while the eyes stay serious during a conversation.
personality: Dominic prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To meet the retired teacher at the bookshop.
family: Jonas Osborne is Dominic’s cousin raised in the same household. Dominic remembers the birthdays. Jonas asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The first delivery fee*, Jonas says, “I am the regular who complained first. I believed the owner paid for delivery all these years.”
connections: Silas Murphy. A retired teacher gets a visit and an apology drafted under the writer's own name.

reactions.situation: A bookseller wants to display the most surprising note
reactions.response: Dominic asks the writer who was supposed to receive the note.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Dominic starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.
